---
title: Membership and roles requirements
id: REQ-MEMBERSHIP
status: approved
owners: [product-team, m.lindqvist]
last_updated: 2026-05-11
related: [REQ-001, REQ-006, ADR-003, DES-011]
---

## Scope

This document defines how a user becomes a member of an organization, what the four roles
mean, how invitations work end to end, and the invariants that keep the last-owner rule and
authored-content ownership consistent under role changes and removals. It does not define
the tenant boundary itself (`organizations.md`) or what each permission action actually
gates on individual resources like issues and comments (`issues.md`,
`comments-and-mentions.md`), though the ownership-escalation mechanic is defined here because
it is a property of roles, not of any one resource.

## Context

Membership is a join between a global `User` (`src/server/repositories/user-repository.ts`,
the one repository that is not tenant-scoped) and an `Organization`, represented as a
`Member` row with a `role`. `src/server/services/member-service.ts` owns role changes and
removal; `src/server/services/invitation-service.ts` owns the invite-and-accept lifecycle
that produces new members. Both call into `src/lib/permissions.ts`, which is the single
authorization entry point (`ADR-003`): `can()`, `assertCan()`, `explain()` and `canAll()`
all read from one `ROLE_MATRIX` table keyed by `PermissionAction`.

The four roles — `owner`, `admin`, `member`, `viewer` — form a strict total order captured
in `ROLE_RANK` (`src/types/member.ts`). `ROLE_MATRIX` records, for every action, the minimum
role required, and `hasRoleAtLeast` is the comparison every "at least this role" check
reduces to. The decision order documented in `permissions.ts` runs cross-tenant guard,
platform-staff bypass, role matrix, then ownership escalation — so a `member` who is not
the assignee of an issue is denied `issue:update` by the matrix, but the same `member` who
authored that issue is granted it by the escalation step that runs after the matrix would
otherwise deny.

Invitations are their own short-lived entity (`src/server/repositories/invitation-repository.ts`),
keyed by a hash of the invite token rather than the plaintext token, so the unauthenticated
accept page (`src/app/(auth)/invite/[token]/page.tsx`) never has to trust a value it cannot
verify against the database. `invitation-service.ts` checks the seat quota
(`wouldExceedLimit`) and the `member:invite` rate-limit bucket before it mints a token,
which is why an org near its seat limit gets `plan_limit_exceeded` before Taskflow ever
writes a pending invitation row it would have to clean up later.

## Open questions

1. `REQ-026`'s ownership escalation list (`issue:update`, `issue:archive`,
   `comment:update`, `comment:delete`, `notification:manage`) is fixed in `permissions.ts`;
   whether project leads (`REQ-049`) should get an analogous escalation for
   `project:update` is an open product question, not yet a requirement.
2. `REQ-027`'s platform-staff bypass has no requirement here describing how staff status is
   granted or revoked — that lives outside this corpus's scope (an internal admin tool).
3. `REQ-032` checks seats at invite time; whether an accepted invitation should re-check the
   seat quota at acceptance time (a window where the quota could have been exhausted by a
   concurrent invite) is unresolved — see the note under `REQ-030`.

### REQ-020 — Four roles form a strict rank order

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** ADR-003, REQ-021, DES-011
- **Implemented by:** `src/types/member.ts` — `ROLE_RANK`, `hasRoleAtLeast`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`, `tests/schemas/member.schema.test.ts`

`ROLE_RANK` in `src/types/member.ts` orders the four roles `owner > admin > member >
viewer`, and every "minimum role" check in the product — `ROLE_MATRIX`, `hasRoleAtLeast`,
the last-owner guard — is expressed against this single ordering rather than an ad hoc set
of role comparisons scattered per feature. There is no fifth role and no per-organization
custom role; Taskflow deliberately does not offer role customization, trading flexibility
for a permission surface simple enough to reason about in one file.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `ROLE_RANK` assigns a strictly increasing numeric rank to `viewer < member < admin <
   owner`.
2. Every comparison of "is this role at least that role" in the codebase goes through
   `hasRoleAtLeast`, not a hand-rolled string comparison.
3. Role values outside the four are rejected at the schema layer (`src/schemas/role.ts`).

### REQ-021 — Role rank determines the default permission decision

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-020, ADR-003, REQ-027

For any `PermissionAction`, `ROLE_MATRIX` declares a minimum role; `can()` compares the
actor's role rank against that minimum after the cross-tenant and platform-staff checks have
already passed. This is the `granted_by_role` / `denied_by_role` branch of `explain()`'s
decision reasons, and it is the default path — most calls to `can()` in the app resolve here
without ever reaching the ownership-escalation step.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `can(actor, action)` returns `true` whenever `actor.role` rank is greater than or equal
   to the action's `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum.
2. `explain()` reports `granted_by_role` or `denied_by_role` for every action not covered
   by an escalation.
3. `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts` sweeps every action against every role.

**Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts`
**Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`

### REQ-022 — Viewers have read-only access across the product

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-020, REQ-181, REQ-224
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `ROLE_MATRIX`, `src/components/domain/permission/permission-gate.tsx`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`, `tests/components/permission-gate.test.tsx`

`viewer` is the minimum role for every `*:read` action in `ROLE_MATRIX` —
`org:read`, `member:read`, `project:read`, `issue:read`, `comment:read`,
`notification:read` — and the minimum role for no mutating action at all. A viewer can open
every screen a member can, but every button that would write is hidden by
`PermissionGate` (see `tests/components/permission-gate.test.tsx`) and, more importantly,
would be denied server-side even if a viewer forged the request.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. No `*:create`, `*:update`, `*:delete`, `*:archive` or `*:manage_*` action's `ROLE_MATRIX`
   minimum is `viewer`.
2. Every `*:read` action's minimum is `viewer` or lower (there is no lower role).
3. A viewer's forged Server Action call is denied server-side regardless of what the client
   rendered.

### REQ-023 — Members may create and edit issues, projects and comments

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-060, REQ-090, REQ-040
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `ROLE_MATRIX`, `src/actions/issues/create-issue.ts`, `src/actions/projects/create-project.ts`, `src/actions/comments/create-comment.ts`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`

`member` is the `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum for `project:create`, `project:update`,
`issue:create`, `issue:update`, `issue:assign`, `issue:archive`, `comment:create` and
`comment:update`. This is the working-contributor role: enough to do the day-to-day job of
running a project and triaging issues, without the organizational authority of `admin`
(inviting people, archiving projects, deleting issues).

**Acceptance criteria**

1. A `member` can call `createIssueAction`, `createProjectAction` and
   `createCommentAction` successfully against a resource in their own org.
2. A `member` calling `deleteIssueAction`-equivalent flows (which require `admin`) is
   denied.
3. A `member`'s issue update to a field they are not the author or assignee of still
   succeeds, because `issue:update`'s matrix minimum is already `member`, independent of
   the ownership escalation in `REQ-026`.

### REQ-024 — Admins manage membership, flags and archiving

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-028, REQ-192, REQ-045
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `ROLE_MATRIX`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`

`admin` is the `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum for `member:invite`, `member:update_role`,
`member:remove`, `org:manage_flags`, `org:update`, `project:archive`, `issue:delete`,
`comment:delete`, `activity:export` and `webhook:manage`. Admins run the organizational side
of the product — who's in it, what's turned on, what gets archived — everything short of
the two owner-only actions (`org:delete`, `org:manage_billing`).

**Acceptance criteria**

1. An `admin` can invite a member, toggle a feature flag and archive a project in one
   session without hitting a permission wall.
2. An `admin` cannot change the plan or delete the organization (`REQ-025`).
3. Every action listed above has `admin` as its exact `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum, not `owner`.

### REQ-025 — Owners alone may delete the organization or change billing

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-007, REQ-140, DES-021
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `ROLE_MATRIX`, `src/actions/billing/change-plan.ts`, `src/actions/billing/update-seats.ts`, `src/actions/billing/cancel-subscription.ts`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`

`org:delete` and `org:manage_billing` are the only two actions whose `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum
is `owner`. Every billing action — `changePlanAction`, `updateSeatsAction`,
`cancelSubscriptionAction` — is gated on `org:manage_billing`, so an `admin` who can do
almost everything else in settings still cannot see or press the change-plan button;
`billing/page.tsx` renders it behind the same `can()` check the server enforces.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `can(actor, 'org:manage_billing')` is `false` for every role below `owner`.
2. `changePlanAction` called by an `admin` returns a `forbidden` `ActionResult`, not a
   silently ignored no-op.
3. The billing settings page hides mutating controls from non-owners but still renders the
   current plan read-only, since `org:read` remains available to everyone.

### REQ-026 — Authors may edit their own issues and comments regardless of rank

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-072, REQ-097, ADR-003

The ownership escalation step runs after the role matrix would otherwise deny: for
`issue:update`, `issue:archive`, `comment:update`, `comment:delete` and
`notification:manage`, an actor who is the resource's author (or, for issues, its assignee)
is granted the action even at a role rank the matrix alone would refuse. This exists because
a `viewer`-turned-`member`'s own issue history and a `member`'s own comments should not
require an `admin` babysitting every edit — self-authored content is a reasonable thing to
let someone maintain regardless of their organizational rank, as long as the action is one
of the five escalation actions and not, say, `issue:delete`.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `explain()` returns `granted_by_ownership` when the matrix would have denied but the
   actor is the author or assignee.
2. Ownership escalation applies to exactly the five actions listed above; it does not apply
   to `issue:delete` or `comment:create`.
3. `tests/lib/permissions.ownership.test.ts` covers both the issue-author and
   issue-assignee escalation paths independently.

**Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts`
**Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.ownership.test.ts`

### REQ-027 — Platform staff bypass the role matrix for support access

- **Priority:** should
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-011, ADR-003, REQ-021
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `can`, `explain`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`, `tests/contract/permissions.test.ts`

`actor.isPlatformStaff` is checked immediately after the cross-tenant guard and before the
role matrix, so a support engineer resolved as an `Actor` for a customer's organization is
granted every action regardless of what role, if any, they hold as a member of that org.
This is deliberately narrower than a global superuser flag: the cross-tenant guard still
runs first, so staff access is always scoped to one organization at a time through the same
`Actor` resolution path everyone else uses, never a backdoor that skips tenancy.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `explain()` returns `granted_by_staff` when `actor.isPlatformStaff` is true, before the
   role matrix is even consulted.
2. Staff bypass does not suppress `denied_cross_tenant`; it only overrides the role matrix.
3. `granted_by_staff` is distinguishable from `granted_by_role` in the decision reason, so
   support-access usage is auditable separately from ordinary admin usage.

### REQ-028 — Invitations are addressed to an email and carry a role

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-024, REQ-032, DES-020
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/invitation-service.ts` — `inviteMember`, `inviteMembers`
- **Verified by:** `tests/services/invitation-service.test.ts`, `tests/schemas/member.schema.test.ts`

`inviteMember` in `src/server/services/invitation-service.ts` takes an email address and a
target role, not a user id — the invited person need not have a Taskflow account yet. The
invitation row records the email, the role it will grant on acceptance, who sent it and when.
`inviteMembers` (plural) exists for the bulk-invite flow on the members settings page,
capped by the bulk-invite bound enforced in `tests/schemas/member.schema.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. An invitation cannot be created for a role higher than the inviting actor's own role
   (an `admin` cannot invite an `owner`).
2. `inviteMembers` enforces the same per-invite checks (seat quota, rate limit) as
   `inviteMember` for each recipient in the batch.
3. Re-inviting an email with a pending invitation updates or resends rather than creating a
   second pending row (`REQ-029`, `resendInvitation`).

### REQ-029 — Invitation tokens are single-use and time-limited

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-030, DES-030, ADR-020
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/invitation-repository.ts` — `findInvitationByTokenHash`, `markInvitationAccepted`, `src/lib/hash.ts` — `hashToken`
- **Verified by:** `tests/services/invitation-service.test.ts`

`invitation-repository.ts` keys lookups on a hash of the token (`hashToken` in
`src/lib/hash.ts`), the same pattern session tokens use (`REQ-203`), so the database never
stores a value that alone lets someone accept the invite. `markInvitationAccepted` records

expiry, is refused by `acceptInvitation` before it ever creates a member.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Accepting an already-accepted invitation fails rather than creating a duplicate member.
2. Accepting an expired invitation fails with a distinct error from an already-accepted
   one.
3. `findInvitationByTokenHash` never receives a plaintext token; the caller hashes first.

### REQ-030 — Accepting an invitation creates a member and emits member.joined

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-006, REQ-111, DES-031
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/invitation-service.ts` — `acceptInvitation`, `src/actions/members/accept-invitation.ts` — `acceptInvitationAction`
- **Verified by:** `tests/services/invitation-service.test.ts`

happy path here does not re-check it — a design trade-off that leaves a narrow window where

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `acceptInvitation` returns a `Member` row whose `role` matches the invitation's recorded
   role, not the caller's request.
2. `member.joined` is emitted exactly once per successful acceptance.
3. `acceptInvitationAction` works for a user who is not yet authenticated as a member of
   any organization, since accepting is how they first join one.

### REQ-031 — The last owner cannot be removed or demoted

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-006, REQ-034, DES-011

`assertLastOwnerRetained(orgId, memberId, nextRole)` in `member-service.ts` runs before both

appeared to succeed but did nothing.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Demoting the sole owner to any other role fails.
2. Removing the sole owner fails, even when the caller is a platform-staff actor.
3. The check counts only active (non-archived) members, so a soft-deleted former owner does
   not block the invariant.

**Implemented by:** `src/server/services/member-service.ts`
**Verified by:** `tests/services/member-service.test.ts`

### REQ-032 — Seat count is checked against the plan before an invite is sent

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-133, REQ-138, ADR-010
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/invitation-service.ts` — `inviteMember`, `src/config/plan-limits.ts` — `wouldExceedLimit`
- **Verified by:** `tests/services/invitation-service.test.ts`, `tests/contract/plan-limits.test.ts`

`inviteMember` calls `wouldExceedLimit(plan, 'seats', usedSeats)` before it writes the
invitation row. A pending invitation counts toward the seat total the same as an accepted

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Inviting past the plan's seat limit fails with `plan_limit_exceeded`, not a database
   constraint error.
2. Pending (unaccepted) invitations are included in the seat count the quota check reads.
3. Revoking a pending invitation frees the seat it was holding.

### REQ-033 — Removing a member preserves their authored content

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** ADR-004, REQ-026, REQ-071
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/member-service.ts` — `removeMember`, `src/server/repositories/user-repository.ts` — `findUsersByIds`
- **Verified by:** `tests/services/member-service.test.ts`

`removeMember` is a soft delete on the member row (`archivePatch`), not a cascade that

   authored.
2. A removed member's `role` on the archived member row is left as it was at removal time,
   for audit purposes.
3. A removed member cannot authenticate an `Actor` for that organization afterward, even
   though their `User` row and past content remain intact.

### REQ-034 — Role changes are audited with before and after values

- **Priority:** should
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-220, REQ-222, ADR-022
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/member-service.ts` — `updateMemberRole`, `src/server/services/activity-service.ts` — `record`
- **Verified by:** `tests/services/member-service.test.ts`

`updateMemberRole` is one of the events that flows into the audit trail: the `activity`

1	---
2	title: Feature flag requirements
3	id: REQ-FLAGS
4	status: approved
5	owners: [product-team, d.okafor]
6	last_updated: 2026-06-02
7	related: [REQ-005, REQ-131, ADR-012, DES-200]
8	---
9	
10	## Scope
11	
12	This document defines the requirements for the feature flag system: the registry, the single
13	evaluation function, the four rollout strategies, plan gating, non-overridable flags,
14	organization-level overrides, the client snapshot, and the closed set of flag keys. It is
15	consumed by nearly every other domain document — `REQ-050` (public projects), `REQ-079`
16	(CSV export), `REQ-120` (digest email), `REQ-136`/`REQ-152` (webhooks), `REQ-175`
17	(advanced search) and `REQ-024`'s issue-templates mention are all specific flags whose
18	general mechanics are defined here rather than repeated per document.
19	
20	## Context
21	
22	`src/config/feature-flags.ts` declares `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`, the one registry every
23	flag is declared in; `src/lib/feature-flags.ts`'s `isEnabled()` is the one function anything
24	in the app — server or client — calls to ask whether a flag is on for a given context, and
25	`snapshotFlags()` is how a server-resolved set of decisions crosses into client components
26	without shipping the registry itself. `feature-flag-service.ts` on the server builds the
27	`FlagContext` (`buildFlagContext`) from the actor and organization, and exposes
28	`getSnapshot`/`toggleFlag` for the settings page and its Server Action.
29	
30	`ADR-012` documents the decision to support exactly four rollout strategies rather than a
31	general rules engine: plan-gated (the flag is on once the org's plan reaches a threshold,
32	per `PLAN_ORDER`), percentage rollout (deterministic per organization, not per user, so a
33	whole organization sees consistent behavior rather than individual members randomly
34	diverging), boolean-always-on (`command_palette`), and role-gated (the flag is on once the
35	acting user's role reaches a threshold, used by `issue_templates`). Every flag in the
36	registry declares exactly one of these strategies plus whether it is `overridable`.
37	
38	Ten flags exist today: `kanban_board` (plan >= starter, overridable), `ai_issue_summary`
39	(percentage 25, overridable), `command_palette` (always on, not overridable),
40	`activity_feed` (plan >= growth, overridable), `public_projects` (plan >= enterprise,
41	overridable), `webhooks` (plan >= growth, not overridable), `csv_export` (plan >= starter,
42	overridable), `digest_email` (plan >= growth, overridable), `issue_templates` (role >=
43	admin, overridable), and `advanced_search` (plan >= enterprise, overridable). `webhooks` and
44	`command_palette` are the only two flags marked not overridable — for `command_palette`
45	because there is no reason to ever turn off a zero-cost client affordance, and for
46	`webhooks` because the plan-tier gate on webhooks is a monetization boundary the product
47	team does not want individual support interactions to erode by ad hoc override.
48	
49	Organization-level overrides live in `Organization.settings` (`REQ-005`, defined in
50	`organizations.md`), which is why this document does not restate the storage location but
51	does define the override's evaluation semantics: an override only takes effect for flags
52	whose definition marks them `overridable`, and `toggleFlag` — the only mutator — requires
53	`org:manage_flags`, whose `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum is `admin`.
54	
55	`src/config/nav.ts`'s `visibleNav` is a second, independent consumer of the flag system worth
56	naming here even though it belongs conceptually to navigation rather than to flags: each
57	`NavItem` optionally names both a `PermissionAction` and a `FeatureFlagKey`, and `visibleNav`
58	filters the sidebar and settings navigation trees by calling both `can()` and `isEnabled()`
59	for every item, so a flagged-off feature's settings link disappears from navigation the same
60	tick the flag itself would refuse the underlying action — there is no separate "hide the
61	nav item" maintenance step distinct from the flag definition driving the behavior it gates.
62	
63	## Open questions
64	
65	1. `REQ-189`'s percentage rollout is deterministic per organization, but this document does
66	   not specify the hashing input beyond "per organization" — whether it is stable across a
67	   flag's own lifetime (so an org does not flip in and out of a 25% rollout as unrelated
68	   registry changes are deployed) is an implementation property not independently pinned
69	   down by a requirement.
70	2. `REQ-187`'s four strategies do not include a strategy that combines two conditions (for
71	   example, plan-gated AND percentage), so a flag needing both would require either two
72	   flags or an ad hoc extension — not currently a real need, but a known limitation of the
73	   registry's shape.
74	3. Whether `toggleFlag`'s audit trail (`REQ-192`) distinguishes an override being set to
75	   `true` versus explicitly set to `false` (forcing a normally-on-by-plan flag off) from an
76	   override simply being cleared is not addressed here.
77	4. The role-gated strategy (`issue_templates`, `admin` minimum) evaluates against the
78	   acting user's role at request time, which raises a question none of the eleven
79	   requirements below directly answers: whether a snapshot taken for a page render should be
80	   invalidated the instant that user's role changes mid-session, or whether it is acceptable
81	   for a stale snapshot to grant access for the remainder of an already-rendered page.
82	
83	### REQ-185 — Flags are declared in a single registry
84	
85	- **Priority:** must
86	- **Status:** implemented
87	- **Related:** ADR-012, REQ-195, DES-200
88	- **Implemented by:** `src/config/feature-flags.ts` — `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`
89	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
90	
91	`FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS` in `src/config/feature-flags.ts` is the only place a flag's key,
92	strategy, and overridability are declared. No service defines its own ad hoc flag check;
93	every gated behavior in the product traces back to one entry in this table.
94	
95	**Acceptance criteria**
96	
97	1. Every `FeatureFlagKey` used anywhere in the codebase has a corresponding entry in
98	   `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`.
99	2. Adding a new gated feature requires exactly one new registry entry, not scattered
100	   conditionals.
101	3. The registry is a plain data structure, not a function, so its contents can be
102	   enumerated and documented without executing code.
103	
104	### REQ-186 — Flag evaluation goes through one function
105	
106	- **Priority:** must
107	- **Status:** implemented
108	- **Related:** REQ-185, DES-200
109	
110	`isEnabled(key, context)` in `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` is the sole evaluator, called from
111	both server code (services, jobs) and client components (through the snapshot, `REQ-194`).
112	No caller re-implements a strategy's logic locally; everything defers to this one function.
113	
114	**Acceptance criteria**
115	
116	1. Every call site checking a flag calls `isEnabled`, not a hand-rolled plan or role
117	   comparison that happens to match a flag's intent.
118	2. `isEnabled` is pure given its inputs — the same `(key, context)` pair always yields the
119	   same result for a given registry state.
120	3. `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts` exercises all four strategies through this one
121	   function.
122	
123	**Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts`
124	**Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
125	
126	### REQ-187 — Four evaluation strategies are supported
127	
128	- **Priority:** must
129	- **Status:** implemented
130	- **Related:** ADR-012, REQ-188, REQ-189
131	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `src/config/feature-flags.ts`
132	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
133	
134	Plan-gated, percentage rollout, always-on, and role-gated are the complete set. Every entry
135	in `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS` declares exactly one; there is no flag with a hybrid or custom
136	strategy, which is the constraint `ADR-012` accepted in exchange for a registry simple enough
137	to audit at a glance.
138	
139	**Acceptance criteria**
140	
141	1. `isEnabled`'s implementation has exactly one branch per strategy kind, exhaustively
142	   covering the strategy union type.
143	2. A flag definition missing a strategy field fails validation at load time rather than
144	   defaulting to some implicit behavior.
145	3. Each of the ten current flags maps to exactly one of the four strategies as documented in
146	   the Context section above.
147	
148	### REQ-188 — Plan-gated flags follow the plan ladder
149	
150	- **Priority:** must
151	- **Status:** implemented
152	- **Related:** REQ-131, REQ-050, REQ-120
153	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `src/config/plan-limits.ts` — `planAtLeast`
154	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
155	
156	A plan-gated flag's threshold is one of the four plan values, and evaluation uses
157	`planAtLeast(org.plan, threshold)` — the same ordering `PLAN_ORDER` establishes for
158	`REQ-131`'s downgrade logic — so a plan-gated flag is automatically consistent with billing's
159	own notion of "higher plan," rather than maintaining an independent comparison.
160	
161	**Acceptance criteria**
162	
163	1. `kanban_board`, `activity_feed`, `public_projects`, `csv_export`, `digest_email` and
164	   `advanced_search` all evaluate via `planAtLeast`.
165	2. An org's plan-gated flag state changes automatically and immediately when
166	   `billing.plan_changed` takes effect, without a separate flag-specific update step.
167	3. `webhooks` is plan-gated at `growth` exactly like `activity_feed` and `digest_email`, but
168	   is additionally marked non-overridable, distinguishing the gating threshold from the
169	   override policy.
170	
171	### REQ-189 — Percentage rollout is deterministic per organization
172	
173	- **Priority:** should
174	- **Status:** implemented
175	- **Related:** REQ-187, DES-210
176	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`
177	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
178	
179	`ai_issue_summary`'s percentage-25 strategy hashes the organization's id (not the acting
180	user's) to decide whether that org falls inside the rollout percentage, so every member of a
181	given organization sees the same on/off state for the flag — there is no scenario where two
182	members of the same org disagree about whether `ai_issue_summary` is available to them
183	because of random per-request evaluation.
184	
185	**Acceptance criteria**
186	
187	1. Repeated evaluations of `isEnabled('ai_issue_summary', context)` for the same
188	   organization return the same result across calls, absent a registry change.
189	2. Two organizations, given a large enough sample, land in the rollout at approximately the
190	   registry's configured percentage.
191	3. The rollout decision does not depend on the acting user, only the organization.
192	
193	### REQ-190 — Some flags are not overridable
194	
195	- **Priority:** must
196	- **Status:** implemented
197	- **Related:** REQ-152, REQ-191, DES-220
198	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` — `toggleFlag`, `buildFlagContext`

209	   by strategy.

216	
217	- **Priority:** must
218	- **Status:** implemented
219	- **Related:** REQ-005, REQ-192
220	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` — `buildFlagContext`

229	**Acceptance criteria**
230	
231	1. An override of `true` on a flag whose plan-gated strategy would otherwise evaluate
232	   `false` results in the flag being enabled for that org.
233	2. An override of `false` on a flag whose strategy would otherwise evaluate `true` results

236	   effect from the cleared value.

238	### REQ-192 — Toggling a flag requires admin and emits flag.toggled
239	
240	- **Priority:** must
241	- **Status:** implemented
242	- **Related:** REQ-024, DES-071
243	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` — `toggleFlag`
244	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
245	
246	`toggleFlag(actor, input)` requires `org:manage_flags` (`admin` minimum) and, on success,
247	emits `flag.toggled` with the flag key and new override value, which the activity service

250	
251	**Acceptance criteria**
252	
253	1. A `member` calling `toggleFeatureFlagAction` is denied regardless of which flag they
254	   target.
255	2. `flag.toggled`'s payload identifies the flag key and the resulting override state

257	3. `toggleFlag` on a non-overridable flag fails before emitting the event (`REQ-190`), since
258	   no actual change occurred.

260	### REQ-193 — A disabled feature fails with FeatureDisabledError
261	
262	- **Priority:** must
263	- **Status:** implemented
264	- **Related:** ADR-014, REQ-138
265	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/errors.ts` — `toAppError`
266	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/errors.test.ts`
267	
268	Attempting a gated action while its flag is off throws `FeatureDisabledError`, mapped by
269	`toAppError` to a distinct, specific `AppErrorShape` — not folded into `forbidden` or
270	`validation_failed` — so a client can distinguish "you don't have permission" from "this
271	isn't available on your plan or hasn't been rolled out to you yet" and render the
272	appropriate upsell or explanation.
273	
274	**Acceptance criteria**
275	
276	1. Every gated Server Action checks `isEnabled` and throws `FeatureDisabledError` rather
277	   than silently no-opping when the flag is off.
278	2. `FeatureDisabledError`'s mapped error code is distinct from `forbidden` and
279	   `plan_limit_exceeded`.
280	3. `tests/lib/errors.test.ts` covers `FeatureDisabledError`'s mapping alongside every other
281	   domain error class.
282	
283	### REQ-194 — The client receives a flag snapshot, not the registry
284	
285	- **Priority:** must
286	- **Status:** implemented
287	- **Related:** REQ-186, DES-230
288	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `snapshotFlags`
289	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
290	
291	`snapshotFlags()` produces a `FeatureFlagSnapshot` — a plain map of flag key to resolved
292	boolean for the current actor and org — that server components pass down to client
293	components, rather than shipping `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS` itself to the browser. This
294	keeps rollout percentages and plan thresholds server-side implementation detail, not
295	something inspectable from client-side JavaScript.
296	
297	**Acceptance criteria**
298	
299	1. No client bundle includes `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS` or the percentage-rollout hash
300	   input.
301	2. `FeatureFlagSnapshot` is computed once per request server-side and passed down, not
302	   recomputed independently by client components calling `isEnabled` themselves with a
303	   client-only context.
304	3. The snapshot reflects the same overrides and strategy evaluation the server would apply
305	   to a Server Action call in the same request.
306	
307	### REQ-195 — Flag keys are a closed union
308	
309	- **Priority:** must
310	- **Status:** implemented
311	- **Related:** REQ-185, DES-200
312	- **Implemented by:** `src/types/feature-flag.ts`, `src/schemas/feature-flag.ts`
313	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
314	
315	`FeatureFlagKey` in `src/types/feature-flag.ts` is a closed string-literal union matching
316	exactly the ten keys in `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`; `src/schemas/feature-flag.ts` validates
317	any client-supplied flag key (for `toggleFeatureFlagAction`'s input) against this same union
318	at runtime, so a request naming an unknown flag key fails validation before it ever reaches
319	`toggleFlag`.
320	
321	**Acceptance criteria**
322	
323	1. `FeatureFlagKey`'s type and `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`'s keys are kept in lockstep; a
324	   registry entry without a corresponding type member is a type error.
325	2. `toggleFeatureFlagSchema` rejects any flag key not in the closed union at the schema
326	   layer, before authorization or business logic runs.
327	3. Adding an eleventh flag requires updating both the type and the registry in the same
328	   change, never one without the other.

title: Feature flag requirements

status: approved
owners: [product-team, d.okafor]
last_updated: 2026-06-02

## Scope

This document defines the requirements for the feature flag system: the registry, the single
evaluation function, the four rollout strategies, plan gating, non-overridable flags,
organization-level overrides, the client snapshot, and the closed set of flag keys. It is
consumed by nearly every other domain document — `REQ-050` (public projects), `REQ-079`
(CSV export), `REQ-120` (digest email), `REQ-136`/`REQ-152` (webhooks), `REQ-175`
(advanced search) and `REQ-024`'s issue-templates mention are all specific flags whose
general mechanics are defined here rather than repeated per document.

## Context

`src/config/feature-flags.ts` declares `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`, the one registry every
flag is declared in; `src/lib/feature-flags.ts`'s `isEnabled()` is the one function anything
in the app — server or client — calls to ask whether a flag is on for a given context, and
`snapshotFlags()` is how a server-resolved set of decisions crosses into client components
without shipping the registry itself. `feature-flag-service.ts` on the server builds the
`FlagContext` (`buildFlagContext`) from the actor and organization, and exposes
`getSnapshot`/`toggleFlag` for the settings page and its Server Action.

`ADR-012` documents the decision to support exactly four rollout strategies rather than a
general rules engine: plan-gated (the flag is on once the org's plan reaches a threshold,
per `PLAN_ORDER`), percentage rollout (deterministic per organization, not per user, so a
whole organization sees consistent behavior rather than individual members randomly
diverging), boolean-always-on (`command_palette`), and role-gated (the flag is on once the
acting user's role reaches a threshold, used by `issue_templates`). Every flag in the
registry declares exactly one of these strategies plus whether it is `overridable`.

Ten flags exist today: `kanban_board` (plan >= starter, overridable), `ai_issue_summary`
(percentage 25, overridable), `command_palette` (always on, not overridable),
`activity_feed` (plan >= growth, overridable), `public_projects` (plan >= enterprise,
overridable), `webhooks` (plan >= growth, not overridable), `csv_export` (plan >= starter,
overridable), `digest_email` (plan >= growth, overridable), `issue_templates` (role >=
admin, overridable), and `advanced_search` (plan >= enterprise, overridable). `webhooks` and
`command_palette` are the only two flags marked not overridable — for `command_palette`
because there is no reason to ever turn off a zero-cost client affordance, and for
`webhooks` because the plan-tier gate on webhooks is a monetization boundary the product
team does not want individual support interactions to erode by ad hoc override.

Organization-level overrides live in `Organization.settings` (`REQ-005`, defined in
`organizations.md`), which is why this document does not restate the storage location but
does define the override's evaluation semantics: an override only takes effect for flags
whose definition marks them `overridable`, and `toggleFlag` — the only mutator — requires
`org:manage_flags`, whose `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum is `admin`.

`src/config/nav.ts`'s `visibleNav` is a second, independent consumer of the flag system worth
naming here even though it belongs conceptually to navigation rather than to flags: each

tick the flag itself would refuse the underlying action — there is no separate "hide the

   example, plan-gated AND percentage), so a flag needing both would require either two

   registry's shape.
3. Whether `toggleFlag`'s audit trail (`REQ-192`) distinguishes an override being set to
   `true` versus explicitly set to `false` (forcing a normally-on-by-plan flag off) from an
   override simply being cleared is not addressed here.

   acting user's role at request time, which raises a question none of the eleven
   requirements below directly answers: whether a snapshot taken for a page render should be
   invalidated the instant that user's role changes mid-session, or whether it is acceptable
   for a stale snapshot to grant access for the remainder of an already-rendered page.

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** ADR-012, REQ-195, DES-200
- **Implemented by:** `src/config/feature-flags.ts` — `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`

- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`

`command_palette` and `webhooks` are marked `overridable: false` in their registry entries;
`toggleFlag` and `buildFlagContext`'s override lookup both must respect this — an override
value stored in `Organization.settings` for a non-overridable flag, however it might get
there, has no effect on evaluation.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `isEnabled` for a non-overridable flag ignores any stored override and evaluates purely
   by strategy.
2. `toggleFlag` on a non-overridable flag key is rejected before it writes anything to
   `Organization.settings`.
3. The distinction between "overridable but currently off" and "not overridable" is visible
   in the flags settings UI, so an admin is not left wondering why a toggle has no effect.

### REQ-191 — Per-organization overrides live in organization settings

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-005, REQ-192
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` — `buildFlagContext`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`

This document is the evaluation-side complement to `REQ-005` in `organizations.md`, which
describes the storage location. Here, the requirement is about precedence: when an override
exists for an overridable flag, `isEnabled` uses the override's value directly rather than
falling through to the strategy evaluation, regardless of what the strategy would have
computed.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. An override of `true` on a flag whose plan-gated strategy would otherwise evaluate
   `false` results in the flag being enabled for that org.
2. An override of `false` on a flag whose strategy would otherwise evaluate `true` results
   in the flag being disabled for that org.
3. Clearing the override reverts evaluation to the underlying strategy, with no residual
   effect from the cleared value.

### REQ-192 — Toggling a flag requires admin and emits flag.toggled

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-024, DES-071
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` — `toggleFlag`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`

`toggleFlag(actor, input)` requires `org:manage_flags` (`admin` minimum) and, on success,
emits `flag.toggled` with the flag key and new override value, which the activity service
records — an important audit trail entry, since a flag override can enable or disable
product surface area for an entire organization in one action.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. A `member` calling `toggleFeatureFlagAction` is denied regardless of which flag they
   target.
2. `flag.toggled`'s payload identifies the flag key and the resulting override state
   (enabled, disabled, or cleared).
3. `toggleFlag` on a non-overridable flag fails before emitting the event (`REQ-190`), since
   no actual change occurred.

### REQ-193 — A disabled feature fails with FeatureDisabledError

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** ADR-014, REQ-138
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/errors.ts` — `toAppError`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/errors.test.ts`

Attempting a gated action while its flag is off throws `FeatureDisabledError`, mapped by
`toAppError` to a distinct, specific `AppErrorShape` — not folded into `forbidden` or
`validation_failed` — so a client can distinguish "you don't have permission" from "this
isn't available on your plan or hasn't been rolled out to you yet" and render the
appropriate upsell or explanation.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Every gated Server Action checks `isEnabled` and throws `FeatureDisabledError` rather
   than silently no-opping when the flag is off.
2. `FeatureDisabledError`'s mapped error code is distinct from `forbidden` and
   `plan_limit_exceeded`.
3. `tests/lib/errors.test.ts` covers `FeatureDisabledError`'s mapping alongside every other
   domain error class.

### REQ-194 — The client receives a flag snapshot, not the registry

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-186, DES-230
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `snapshotFlags`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`

`snapshotFlags()` produces a `FeatureFlagSnapshot` — a plain map of flag key to resolved
boolean for the current actor and org — that server components pass down to client
components, rather than shipping `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS` itself to the browser. This
keeps rollout percentages and plan thresholds server-side implementation detail, not
something inspectable from client-side JavaScript.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. No client bundle includes `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS` or the percentage-rollout hash
   input.
2. `FeatureFlagSnapshot` is computed once per request server-side and passed down, not
   recomputed independently by client components calling `isEnabled` themselves with a
   client-only context.
3. The snapshot reflects the same overrides and strategy evaluation the server would apply
   to a Server Action call in the same request.

### REQ-195 — Flag keys are a closed union

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-185, DES-200
- **Implemented by:** `src/types/feature-flag.ts`, `src/schemas/feature-flag.ts`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`

`FeatureFlagKey` in `src/types/feature-flag.ts` is a closed string-literal union matching
exactly the ten keys in `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`; `src/schemas/feature-flag.ts` validates
any client-supplied flag key (for `toggleFeatureFlagAction`'s input) against this same union
at runtime, so a request naming an unknown flag key fails validation before it ever reaches
`toggleFlag`.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `FeatureFlagKey`'s type and `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`'s keys are kept in lockstep; a
   registry entry without a corresponding type member is a type error.
2. `toggleFeatureFlagSchema` rejects any flag key not in the closed union at the schema
   layer, before authorization or business logic runs.
3. Adding an eleventh flag requires updating both the type and the registry in the same
   change, never one without the other.

18	
19	- **Route:** `/{orgSlug}/settings/billing`
20	- **Files:** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/billing/page.tsx`
21	- **Server or client:** Server Component shell, plan-selection cards are interactive

23	  `brief-common.md`) — 404 otherwise
24	- **Feature flag:** none
25	- **Data loaded:** `getBillingSummary(actor, org.id)` (`src/server/services/billing-service.ts`)
26	- **Components:** `BillingPlanCard` (`src/components/domain/billing/billing-plan-card.tsx`),
27	  `UsagePanel`
28	- **Actions invoked:** `changePlanAction` (`src/actions/billing/change-plan.ts`)
29	- **Satisfies:** REQ-130, REQ-131, REQ-140, REQ-141, REQ-142
30	- **Design:** DES-135, DES-136
31	
32	### Layout
33	
34	A header showing seats-on-plan and subscription status, a link to the invoice history route, a
35	"Usage" section rendering the full `UsagePanel` (identical component to the one on the org
36	overview, reused verbatim — see `screen-org-home.md`), and a "Plans" section: a two-column grid
37	of `BillingPlanCard`s, one per entry in `PLAN_IDS` (`src/types/billing.ts`), each rendered from
38	`getPlanLimits(plan)` so the numbers shown for every tier — free, starter, growth, enterprise —
39	come from the exact same `PlanLimits` table the quota guards elsewhere in the app enforce
40	against, never a separately maintained marketing copy of those numbers. A footer note under the
41	plan grid states the downgrade rule plainly: "Downgrading is refused while usage still exceeds
42	the target plan — free up seats or projects first."
43	
44	### Downgrades are checked against the target plan's limits before the switch
45	
46	`DES-136` is the design fact this screen's downgrade behavior visualizes: before a plan change
47	takes effect, every summary resource (seats, projects, issues, storage, API requests, webhooks)
48	is checked against the *target* plan's limits, not the current one — an org sitting at 40 seats
49	cannot downgrade to starter (10 seats) no matter how the request is framed, and the check runs
50	for the whole resource set at once rather than seat-by-seat. This page has no client-side
51	pre-check of its own; `selectPlan()` is a thin `"use server"` wrapper around `changePlanAction`,
52	so a downgrade attempt that would violate a limit surfaces only as the generic action error
53	`BillingPlanCard`'s `onSelect` handler receives — there is no separate warning rendered before
54	the click, which means an org close to a downgrade boundary discovers the refusal only by
55	attempting it. `REQ-141` is the requirement this enforces, and `REQ-140` is the companion
56	requirement covering the success path: a plan change, once accepted, emits `billing.plan_changed`.
57	
58	### SCR-021 — Invoices
59	
60	- **Route:** `/{orgSlug}/settings/billing/invoices`
61	- **Files:** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/billing/invoices/page.tsx`
62	- **Server or client:** Server Component
63	- **Permission required:** `org:manage_billing`, the identical gate the billing page uses — the
64	  page's own doc comment notes this is deliberate, since invoices carry amounts and are not
65	  something a member should be able to browse even read-only
66	- **Feature flag:** none
67	- **Data loaded:** `listInvoices(actor, org.id)`
68	- **Components:** `InvoiceTable` (`src/components/domain/billing/invoice-table.tsx`),
69	  `EmptyState`
70	- **Actions invoked:** none — purely a read screen
71	- **Satisfies:** REQ-143
72	- **Design:** none directly at the design-doc layer beyond the billing service's general
73	  invoice generation coverage
74	
75	A single flat table, one row per billing period, newest first. `REQ-143` (invoices generated per
76	billing period) is the requirement this table visualizes; a free-plan org sees an `EmptyState`
77	("No invoices yet — Organizations on the free plan are never invoiced") since free orgs never
78	accrue a billed period in the first place.
79	
80	## SCR-022 — Feature flags
81	
82	- **Route:** `/{orgSlug}/settings/flags`
83	- **Files:** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/flags/page.tsx`, list in
84	  `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/flags/flag-toggle-list.tsx`
85	- **Server or client:** Server Component shell, interactive toggle list
86	- **Permission required:** `org:manage_flags` (member and above) — 404 otherwise
87	- **Feature flag:** n/a — this page *is* the flag-management surface, not something a flag
88	  gates
89	- **Data loaded:** no service call beyond tenant context; the ten rows are built in-memory from
90	  `Object.values(FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS)` (`src/config/feature-flags.ts`) combined with
91	  `isEnabled()` evaluated once per flag and `org.settings.enabledFlagOverrides` (a `Set`) for
92	  the override state
93	- **Components:** `FlagToggleList`
94	- **Actions invoked:** `toggleFeatureFlagAction` (`src/actions/flags/toggle-flag.ts`)
95	- **Satisfies:** REQ-185, REQ-188, REQ-190, REQ-191, REQ-192
96	- **Design:** DES-175, DES-176, DES-177
97	
98	### Three separate facts per row, deliberately not conflated
99	
100	This page's own doc comment names the exact design tension it resolves: each row shows three
101	things that are easy to collapse into one but are not the same fact — what the flag definition's
102	*rollout strategy* says (rendered via a local `describeStrategy()` helper mapping `on`/`off`/
103	`plan`/`role`/`percentage` to plain-English labels: "Always on," "Off by default," "Included from
104	a certain plan," "Limited by role," "Percentage rollout"), whether the *organization has an
105	override* set (`overridden`, from the `enabledFlagOverrides` set), and what `isEnabled()`
106	*actually evaluates to right now* (`enabled`, which folds the override, the strategy, and the
107	org's current plan/role context together). A row can show "Included from a certain plan" as its
108	strategy while still showing `enabled: false` if the org's current plan does not meet the
109	threshold, and a row can show `enabled: true` purely because of an override even though its
110	strategy alone would evaluate false — the three columns exist precisely so an admin can tell
111	those cases apart rather than only seeing the final boolean.
112

114	`FlagToggleList` — `command_palette` and `webhooks` are both `NOT overridable` per

116	viewing admin's role. `DES-177` is the authorization fact behind the toggle itself: `toggleFlag`
117	checks overridability against the *registry*, not against role rank — an admin cannot force an
118	override onto a non-overridable flag no matter how the request is crafted, because the guard is a
119	property of the flag definition, not a permission check that a higher role could satisfy. `REQ-192`
120	requires that a successful toggle emits `flag.toggled`, and `DES-177` adds that the emitted event
121	carries a *re-evaluation* of the result rather than trusting whatever the client requested —

123	client's intent.

126	
127	- **Route:** `/{orgSlug}/settings/webhooks`
128	- **Files:** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/webhooks/page.tsx`, manager in
129	  `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/webhooks/webhook-manager.tsx`
130	- **Server or client:** Server Component shell, interactive manager
131	- **Permission required:** `webhook:manage` (admin and above) — 404 when absent
132	- **Feature flag:** `webhooks` (plan >= growth, **not** overridable)

134	  org.id)` (`src/server/services/webhook-service.ts`) — but only once the flag check passes
135	- **Components:** `WebhookManager`, `EmptyState`
136	- **Actions invoked:** `createWebhookAction` (`src/actions/webhooks/create-webhook.ts`),
137	  `deleteWebhookAction` (`src/actions/webhooks/delete-webhook.ts`)

139	- **Design:** DES-159, DES-160, DES-161, DES-257, DES-258

141	### Three gates, and only the first one is a wall
142	
143	This page's own doc comment lays out its gating order deliberately: permission (`webhook:manage`
144	— may you manage webhooks at all), flag (`webhooks` — is the surface available on this plan),
145	and quota (`endpoints.length >= limits.webhooks` — how many more you may add). Only the first is
146	a hard `notFound()`; the other two render as *explanations* rather than blocking navigation. A
147	disabled `webhooks` flag produces an `EmptyState` ("Webhooks are not part of this plan — Upgrade
148	in Settings → Billing…") and skips `listWebhooks` entirely, identical in shape to the
149	`activity_feed` gate documented in `screen-activity.md`. A reached quota does not block the page
150	from rendering at all — `WebhookManager` receives `atLimit={endpoints.length >= limits.webhooks}`
151	as a prop and is expected to disable its own "add endpoint" affordance internally, so existing
152	endpoints remain fully manageable (editable, deletable, testable) even once the org can create no
153	more.
154	
155	`DES-257` is the design fact that explains why this page checks the flag and the quota as two
156	genuinely independent conditions rather than deriving one from the other: an *override* can force
157	the flag on without touching the numeric ceiling, since `webhooks` (the flag) governs whether the
158	feature surface exists at all while `limits.webhooks` (the quota, from `PlanLimits`) governs how
159	many endpoints the plan permits — a growth-plan org with the flag on by its normal plan gate and
160	a starter-plan org with the flag force-enabled by an override face the same quota math once
161	they're both past the flag check, because the quota is read straight from `getPlanLimits(org.plan)`
162	regardless of how the flag itself was satisfied.
163	
164	### Secret minted once, never regenerated
165	
166	`DES-159` documents a fact this screen's create flow depends on but does not surface visually
167	beyond a one-time reveal (handled inside `WebhookManager`, not this page): an endpoint's signing
168	secret is minted exactly once at creation and never regenerated — there is no "rotate secret"
169	action anywhere in the manifest for this screen, `create-webhook.ts` and `delete-webhook.ts` are
170	the only two mutations wired here. `DES-258` explains why `deleteWebhookAction` is deliberately
171	**not** flag-gated the way creation is: a downgraded organization that has lost the `webhooks`
172	flag must still be able to clean up its existing endpoints, so delete works even when the create
173	button and the rest of the page's normal content have already fallen back to the "not part of
174	this plan" `EmptyState` — practically, this means an org that downgrades below growth still needs
175	some path back into this page to delete stale endpoints, which the flag-off `EmptyState` as
176	currently written does not obviously provide, since the whole manager (delete button included)
177	is skipped when the flag check fails before `listWebhooks` ever runs. This is a known rough edge
178	worth flagging rather than glossing over: the design intent (`DES-258`) and the page's literal
179	control flow (flag-off short-circuits to `EmptyState` before the manager renders at all) do not
180	fully agree, and reconciling them is open in the same ops backlog referenced in
181	`screen-search.md`'s notes on copy/behavior drift.

183	### States
184	
185	| state | screen | trigger | what the user sees |
186	|---|---|---|---|
187	| empty | invoices | zero invoices, typically a free-plan org | `EmptyState`: "No invoices yet" |
188	| loading | all four | client navigation | `[orgSlug]/loading.tsx` — none of these four define a dedicated `loading.tsx` |
189	| error | all four | thrown error resolving tenant context or a service call | `[orgSlug]/error.tsx` |
190	| permission denied | all four | `org:manage_billing` / `org:manage_flags` / `webhook:manage` fails | `notFound()` |
191	| flag off | webhooks | `webhooks` flag false for the org's plan | `EmptyState`: "Webhooks are not part of this plan," no endpoint list fetched |
192	| plan limit reached | billing | downgrade target plan's limits exceeded by current usage | Generic action error on `selectPlan()`, no pre-emptive client-side warning |
193	| plan limit reached | webhooks | `endpoints.length >= limits.webhooks` | `WebhookManager` renders existing endpoints normally; its create control is disabled via `atLimit` |

- **Server or client:** Server Component shell, interactive manager
- **Permission required:** `webhook:manage` (admin and above) — 404 when absent
- **Feature flag:** `webhooks` (plan >= growth, **not** overridable)
- **Data loaded:** `getPlanLimits(org.plan)` for the endpoint ceiling, `listWebhooks(actor,
  org.id)` (`src/server/services/webhook-service.ts`) — but only once the flag check passes
- **Components:** `WebhookManager`, `EmptyState`
- **Actions invoked:** `createWebhookAction` (`src/actions/webhooks/create-webhook.ts`),
  `deleteWebhookAction` (`src/actions/webhooks/delete-webhook.ts`)
- **Satisfies:** REQ-150, REQ-151, REQ-152, REQ-153, REQ-159, REQ-161
- **Design:** DES-159, DES-160, DES-161, DES-257, DES-258

### Three gates, and only the first one is a wall

This page's own doc comment lays out its gating order deliberately: permission (`webhook:manage`
— may you manage webhooks at all), flag (`webhooks` — is the surface available on this plan),
and quota (`endpoints.length >= limits.webhooks` — how many more you may add). Only the first is
a hard `notFound()`; the other two render as *explanations* rather than blocking navigation. A
disabled `webhooks` flag produces an `EmptyState` ("Webhooks are not part of this plan — Upgrade
in Settings → Billing…") and skips `listWebhooks` entirely, identical in shape to the
`activity_feed` gate documented in `screen-activity.md`. A reached quota does not block the page
from rendering at all — `WebhookManager` receives `atLimit={endpoints.length >= limits.webhooks}`
as a prop and is expected to disable its own "add endpoint" affordance internally, so existing
endpoints remain fully manageable (editable, deletable, testable) even once the org can create no
more.

`DES-257` is the design fact that explains why this page checks the flag and the quota as two
genuinely independent conditions rather than deriving one from the other: an *override* can force
the flag on without touching the numeric ceiling, since `webhooks` (the flag) governs whether the
feature surface exists at all while `limits.webhooks` (the quota, from `PlanLimits`) governs how
many endpoints the plan permits — a growth-plan org with the flag on by its normal plan gate and
a starter-plan org with the flag force-enabled by an override face the same quota math once
they're both past the flag check, because the quota is read straight from `getPlanLimits(org.plan)`
regardless of how the flag itself was satisfied.

### Secret minted once, never regenerated

`DES-159` documents a fact this screen's create flow depends on but does not surface visually
beyond a one-time reveal (handled inside `WebhookManager`, not this page): an endpoint's signing
secret is minted exactly once at creation and never regenerated — there is no "rotate secret"
action anywhere in the manifest for this screen, `create-webhook.ts` and `delete-webhook.ts` are
the only two mutations wired here. `DES-258` explains why `deleteWebhookAction` is deliberately
**not** flag-gated the way creation is: a downgraded organization that has lost the `webhooks`
flag must still be able to clean up its existing endpoints, so delete works even when the create
button and the rest of the page's normal content have already fallen back to the "not part of
this plan" `EmptyState` — practically, this means an org that downgrades below growth still needs
some path back into this page to delete stale endpoints, which the flag-off `EmptyState` as
currently written does not obviously provide, since the whole manager (delete button included)
is skipped when the flag check fails before `listWebhooks` ever runs. This is a known rough edge
worth flagging rather than glossing over: the design intent (`DES-258`) and the page's literal
control flow (flag-off short-circuits to `EmptyState` before the manager renders at all) do not
fully agree, and reconciling them is open in the same ops backlog referenced in
`screen-search.md`'s notes on copy/behavior drift.

### States

| state | screen | trigger | what the user sees |
|---|---|---|---|
| empty | invoices | zero invoices, typically a free-plan org | `EmptyState`: "No invoices yet" |
| loading | all four | client navigation | `[orgSlug]/loading.tsx` — none of these four define a dedicated `loading.tsx` |
| error | all four | thrown error resolving tenant context or a service call | `[orgSlug]/error.tsx` |
| permission denied | all four | `org:manage_billing` / `org:manage_flags` / `webhook:manage` fails | `notFound()` |
| flag off | webhooks | `webhooks` flag false for the org's plan | `EmptyState`: "Webhooks are not part of this plan," no endpoint list fetched |
| plan limit reached | billing | downgrade target plan's limits exceeded by current usage | Generic action error on `selectPlan()`, no pre-emptive client-side warning |
| plan limit reached | webhooks | `endpoints.length >= limits.webhooks` | `WebhookManager` renders existing endpoints normally; its create control is disabled via `atLimit` |

11

13	`withAction()` and all three ask `can()` about a `PermissionResource` shaped like
14	`{ kind: "comment", orgId, commentId, authorId }`, which is how comment permissions apply
15	the same ownership-escalation pattern issues use — `authorId` compared against
16	`actor.userId` is what lets a member edit or delete their own comment even though
17	`comment:update`/`comment:delete` sit at member/admin rank respectively in `ROLE_MATRIX`.
18	
19	## `createCommentAction`
20	
21	- **File:** `src/actions/comments/create-comment.ts`
22	- **Input schema:** `createCommentSchema` (`src/schemas/comment.ts`) — `CreateCommentInput`
23	- **Returns:** `ActionResult<Comment>`
24	- **Permission:** `comment:create` (minimum role member; see DES-043)
25	- **Feature flag:** none
26	- **Rate limit bucket:** `comment:create` (capacity 60, refill 10/min)
27	- **Plan limit:** none
28	- **Events emitted:** `comment.created` with mentioned user ids (via `createComment()`)
29	- **Cache tags revalidated:** `issueTag(input.issueId)`, `CACHE_PROFILES.seconds`
30	- **Errors:** `validation_failed`, `forbidden`, `rate_limited`, `internal_error`
31	- **Satisfies:** REQ-090, REQ-091, REQ-095, REQ-096
32	- **Design:** DES-115, DES-116, DES-238
33	
34	### Input fields
35	
36	| field | type | required | notes |
37	|---|---|---|---|
38	| `orgId` | branded `OrgId` | yes | |
39	| `issueId` | branded `IssueId` | yes | |
40	| `body` | string, 1-10000 | yes | Markdown, a restricted subset per REQ-091 |
41	| `parentId` | branded `CommentId` or `null` | no, default `null` | reply-to relation |
42	| `mentionedUserIds` | array of branded `UserId`, max 50 | no, default `[]` | client-side parse of `@mentions`; the server re-parses and its own list wins on disagreement (DES-116) |
43	
44	### Behaviour
45	
46	`can(actor, "comment:create", { commentId: PENDING_COMMENT_ID, authorId: actor.userId, ...
47	})` runs first — DES-238 states explicitly that the rate-limit bucket is charged **only
48	after** this permission check succeeds, not before. This is the opposite ordering from
49	`loginAction`'s rate-limit-first pattern in `actions-auth.md`, and the reason is different
50	too: there is no enumeration concern here (the caller is already an authenticated member of
51	the org), so there is no reason to burn a token-bucket charge on a request that was going to
52	be rejected on permission grounds regardless. Only once `comment:create` passes does
53	`consumeRateLimit(input.orgId, "comment:create")` run, throwing `RateLimitedError` on a
54	refused verdict.
55	
56	DES-115 documents the deeper reason this ordering matters at the service layer, one level
57	below this action: comment creation is rate limited **before** mentions are resolved, so a
58	burst of comment submissions never reaches the member-scanning code path that resolves
59	`@mentions` into real user ids — a caller hammering the endpoint gets throttled cheaply,
60	before the more expensive mention-resolution work runs at all. DES-116 is the other half:
61	mentions are resolved server-side, and the server's own list wins on disagreement with the
62	client — the `mentionedUserIds` field in the payload is treated as a hint, not a source of
63	truth; `CommentService` re-parses the `body` for `@mentions` itself and the notification
64	fan-out (REQ-095, `comment.created` carrying mentioned user ids) uses the server's
65	recomputed list. This exists because a client-side mention parser can be tricked (or can
66	simply be stale relative to a body edited after the mention picker ran) in a way that would
67	let a comment notify — or fail to notify — the wrong set of people if the server trusted it.
68	
69	## `updateCommentAction`
70	
71	- **File:** `src/actions/comments/update-comment.ts`
72	- **Input schema:** `updateCommentSchema` (`src/schemas/comment.ts`) — `UpdateCommentInput`
73	- **Returns:** `ActionResult<Comment>`
74	- **Permission:** `comment:update` (minimum role member, with author escalation; see DES-041)
75	- **Feature flag:** none
76	- **Rate limit bucket:** none
77	- **Plan limit:** none
78	- **Events emitted:** none — see DES-120 below
79	- **Cache tags revalidated:** `["comments"]` (static tag only; no `issueTag` call here — see
80	  "A cache-invalidation asymmetry" below)
81	- **Errors:** `validation_failed`, `forbidden`, `internal_error`
82	- **Satisfies:** REQ-097, REQ-102
83	- **Design:** DES-117, DES-239
84	
85	### Input fields
86	
87	| field | type | required | notes |
88	|---|---|---|---|
89	| `orgId` | branded `OrgId` | yes | |
90	| `commentId` | branded `CommentId` | yes | |
91	| `body` | string, 1-10000 | yes | full replacement, not a partial patch |
92	
93	### Behaviour
94	
95	The `can()` check here passes `authorId: actor.userId` — the caller's own id, standing in
96	for "assume I am the author" — which the file's own comment names as deliberately
97	**optimistic**: it is a pre-check made with the caller as the presumed author, so a viewer
98	(who has no `comment:update` grant at all under the role matrix, and whose id will not
99	match the real `authorId` even if it did) is rejected before the round trip to the service.
100	The check that actually enforces "only your own comments" is a second one, inside
101	`CommentService.updateComment`, which repeats the permission check against the row's
102	*persisted* `authorId` after it has been fetched — DES-239. This two-layer check exists
103	because the action layer has no cheap way to know the real author without a database read it
104	would rather not do just to fail fast for the common, correctly-rejected case (a viewer with
105	no update grant at all, who is rejected by role rank alone, no author check needed).
106	
107	DES-117: the self-edit window only applies to the author, and closes fifteen minutes after
108	posting — a detail enforced at the service layer, not visible in this action file at all,
109	but worth knowing when a user reports "I can't edit my own comment anymore" only a few
110	minutes after seeing the edit control. DES-120: editing a comment does **not** re-run mention
111	resolution or re-emit an event — unlike creation, an edited comment's body is not re-scanned
112	for new `@mentions`, and no `comment.updated` (there is no such key in `TaskflowEventMap`
113	either) or other event fires, which is why the "Events emitted" line above is `none`.
114	
115	**A cache-invalidation asymmetry.** `createCommentAction` and `deleteCommentAction` both
116	revalidate `issueTag(...)` for the specific issue the comment belongs to, in addition to the
117	static `["comments"]` tag `withAction()` invalidates. `updateCommentAction` revalidates only
118	the static tag — it does not call `revalidateTagged([issueTag(...)], ...)` itself, even
119	though an edited comment's body is exactly the kind of change a reader on the issue detail
120	page would want to see promptly. This is not documented as intentional in the source; it
121	reads as an inconsistency worth flagging in review rather than a deliberate design decision,
122	and a reader debugging "my comment edit doesn't show up until the page is reloaded" should
123	look here first.
124	
125	## `deleteCommentAction`
126	
127	- **File:** `src/actions/comments/delete-comment.ts`
128	- **Input schema:** `deleteCommentSchema` (`src/schemas/comment.ts`) — `DeleteCommentInput`
129	- **Returns:** `ActionResult<Comment>`
130	- **Permission:** `comment:delete` (minimum role admin, with author escalation; see DES-041)
131	- **Feature flag:** none
132	- **Rate limit bucket:** none
133	- **Plan limit:** none
134	- **Events emitted:** `comment.deleted` (via `deleteComment()`)
135	- **Cache tags revalidated:** `issueTag(comment.issueId)`, `CACHE_PROFILES.seconds`
136	- **Errors:** `validation_failed`, `forbidden`, `internal_error`
137	- **Satisfies:** REQ-098, REQ-099, REQ-100, REQ-101
138	- **Design:** DES-118, DES-240
139	
140	### Input fields
141	
142	| field | type | required | notes |
143	|---|---|---|---|
144	| `orgId` | branded `OrgId` | yes | |
145	| `commentId` | branded `CommentId` | yes | |
146	
147	### Behaviour
148	
149	`comment:delete` sits at admin rank in `ROLE_MATRIX`, but the `authorId: actor.userId` field
150	in the `can()` call gives the same ownership escalation the update action has — an author
151	below admin rank may still delete their own comment. DES-240: deletion is a soft delete, so
152	reply chains keep their parent — `CommentService` stamps `archived_at` through
153	`archivePatch()` rather than removing the row, which matters because a deleted comment might
154	have replies hanging off it, and a hard delete would either orphan those replies (dangling
155	`parentId`) or require cascading the delete into them, which the corpus does not do for
156	comments the way `deleteLabelAction` cascades into the label join table. Comment threads keep
157	archived replies for the same reason (DES-186, at the repository layer) — the thread render
158	filters archived comments out of the visible list (REQ-101) but the row, and the parent
159	pointer it needs to keep a still-visible reply correctly nested, survives.
160	
161	DES-118 adds a timing detail: the `comment.deleted` event's timestamp is taken from the
162	archive patch, not from a fresh clock read at emission time — `archivePatch()` computes
163	`archived_at` once, and both the persisted column and the event payload's `occurredAt` derive
164	from that same value, so there is no window in which the row's stored timestamp and the
165	event's reported timestamp could disagree even by a few milliseconds of scheduling jitter
166	between the write and the `emit()` call.
167	
168	## Comment creation sequence
169	
170	```mermaid
171	sequenceDiagram
172	    participant Form as comment composer
173	    participant Action as createCommentAction
174	    participant Perm as can()
175	    participant RL as consumeRateLimit()
176	    participant Svc as CommentService.createComment()
177	    participant Bus as event-bus emit("comment.created")
178	    participant Notif as NotificationService (subscriber)
179	
180	    Form->>Action: createCommentAction({ issueId, body, mentionedUserIds })
181	    Action->>Action: createCommentSchema.safeParse(raw)
182	    Action->>Perm: can(actor, "comment:create", { commentId: PENDING_COMMENT_ID, authorId })
183	    alt not allowed
184	        Perm-->>Action: false
185	        Action-->>Form: { ok: false, error: { code: "forbidden" } }
186	    else allowed
187	        Perm-->>Action: true
188	        Action->>RL: consumeRateLimit(orgId, "comment:create")
189	        alt throttled
190	            RL-->>Action: { allowed: false }
191	            Action-->>Form: { ok: false, error: { code: "rate_limited" } }
192	        else allowed
193	            RL-->>Action: { allowed: true }
194	            Action->>Svc: createComment(actor, input)
195	            Svc->>Svc: re-parse body for @mentions (server list wins)
196	            Svc->>Bus: emit("comment.created", { mentionedUserIds, ... })
197	            Bus-->>Notif: fan-out (async, isolated per handler)
198	            Svc-->>Action: Comment
199	            Action-->>Form: { ok: true, data: comment }
200	        end
201	    end
202	```
203	
204	## Why comments have no soft-delete restore action
205	
206	Unlike issues and projects, src/actions/comments/ has no `restore-comment.ts`. This is
207	consistent with `updateCommentSchema` and `deleteCommentSchema` being the entire comment
208	mutation surface beyond creation: a deleted comment is, per DES-240, filtered out of thread
209	reads but its row survives, which is enough to satisfy REQ-098 (deletion is a soft delete)
210	without requiring a UI path back. If a deleted comment needs to reappear, that is currently
211	an operator-level database fix rather than a self-service action — a gap worth knowing about
212	rather than assuming a hidden restore path exists somewhere in the settings surface.
213	
214	## Rank asymmetry between update and delete
215	
216	`comment:update` sits at member rank and `comment:delete` at admin rank in `ROLE_MATRIX`,
217	even though both carry the same author-ownership escalation. In practice this means an
218	ordinary member can always edit their own comment (member rank already grants
219	`comment:update` regardless of authorship) but can delete only their own — a member who is
220	not the author of a given comment has no path to deleting it, while an admin can delete any
221	comment in the organization regardless of who wrote it. The asymmetry mirrors the general
222	shape of `ROLE_MATRIX`: editing content is treated as an ordinary collaborative action,
223	removing it as a moderation action that defaults to admin oversight unless the remover is
224	also the author.
225	
226	## Reading a thread versus mutating it
227	
228	None of the three actions documented here is a "read" action — listing a thread is a
229	Server Component concern reading through `getThread()` at the service layer, not a Server
230	Action, and DES-119 notes that `getThread` re-checks `comment:read` even though the caller
231	already proved they can read the parent issue, a small extra permission call that costs
232	little and closes a theoretical gap where issue-read and comment-read diverge in some future
233	change to `ROLE_MATRIX`. It is worth stating plainly for anyone hunting for a
234	`listCommentsAction`: it does not exist. `listCommentsSchema` in `src/schemas/comment.ts`
235	backs a Server Component data fetch, not a client-invoked mutation, which is why it has no
236	entry in this file — this document only covers the three Server Actions the comment domain
237	actually exposes.
238	
239	Related: REQ-092, REQ-093, REQ-094, DES-119, DES-121, DES-126, ADR-009, ADR-014.
240
